Our bags were packed on the last afternoon of term. Everyone was ready to leave when Ms Lane wheeled in a trolley. Its large box was marked "Lost Things". We were to help return them before the holidays.

First came a red glove. Nobody claimed it. Then Ms Lane held up its partner. "A complete pair!" called Kim. She recognised them at once. She had searched her bag for weeks without asking at the office.

There were bottles, pencil cases and a very small shoe. Ms Lane did not ask us to guess their owners. She told us to check names and other details.

A blue bottle looked like mine, but the name underneath was different from mine. I left it there. Beside it, I found my old green one with its broken lid. I had thought someone had thrown it away.

The shoe was too small for anyone in our class. We examined it carefully but found no name. Jo remembered our autumn play. The shoe belonged to a puppet, not a student. She fetched the puppet, and the shoe fitted perfectly. Everyone laughed.

We sorted things into boxes for different classrooms. Unknown items would remain at the office for collection. By the bell, the big box was nearly empty. Ms Lane thanked us, but Kim held up her gloves. "We helped ourselves, too," she said.

I took my bottle home. Dad found a spare lid that fitted, so I could use it again. Next term, I wrote my name on both parts.

Our class also made a sign showing where lost property was kept. It did not promise that nothing would ever go missing. It simply made finding things easier. Whenever I saw that trolley, I remembered the puppet's shoe and smiled, instead of thinking of a boring afternoon.
